title: Constant/limit ringed sequence projection and coherent reduction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be sheaves of commutative rings with strict transition maps $q_{m,n}$ for $m\ge n\ge1$, and put $B=\varprojlim_n B_n$, with projections $\rho_n$. On $\mathcal V=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ put arrows $(V,k)\to(U,n)$ for $V\to U$ and $k\le n$, and the topology generated by coverings at a fixed index. Let $C_\bullet(U,n)=B_n(U)$, with horizontal restriction $q_{m,n}$, and let $\mathscr S(B_\bullet)$ be the category of strict semilinear module systems [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. There is a canonical exact equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal V}(C_\bullet)\simeq\mathscr S(B_\bullet)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The constant-sequence functor and inverse limit form the inverse/direct-image adjunction of a geometric morphism $\pi:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], equipped with the ring map $\pi^{-1}B\to C_\bullet$ whose components are $\rho_n$.

On ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $L\pi^*$ is triangulated and for any flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] is represented by the single strict system $(P\otimes_B B_n)_n$ with transitions $1\otimes q_{m,n}$. These identifications are natural on derived morphisms. In particular its evaluation at $n$ is canonically $K\otimes_B^L B_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and its quotient maps compose before localization. Restriction at each level along $\rho_n$ defines an exact functor $U:\mathscr S(B_\bullet)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ [def-weil-inverse-system, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; it retains the actual underlying additive transitions.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), constant/limit geometric morphism; Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), its K-flat pullback. The varying-ring module identification is the implicit prerequisite extracted here.

proof.text: Use the recorded semilinear realization: Systems is definitionally the sequence-site module category. The completion equivalence is the identity and therefore preserves finite limits and finite colimits. The underlying strict-system realization is the existing vertical-restriction equivalence.

Restrict a set sheaf to each vertical slice and retain its horizontal restrictions. Constant sequences are sheaves because gluing on a fixed-index covering is gluing on the base site; separatedness after pullback checks arbitrary product arrows. Compatible slice maps are precisely cones. Limit lifting gives the forward Hom map and its coordinate projections give the inverse. Their coordinate equations prove both inverse laws and naturality. The forgetful sheaf functor reflects limits and computes them sectionwise, so the constant functor preserves finite limits.

Restrict every level along the cone projection. The cone naturality equation makes the unchanged horizontal restrictions linear over the cone ring. This defines an additive functor into the tower of base-ring modules. Evaluation is exact and scalar restriction is exact, so evaluations detect preservation of finite limits and colimits. The underlying-set functor preserves tower limits; its canonical limit comparison identifies the module direct image with the set direct image. The cone projections define the structural ring map. Ring-map identities and module linearity hold on coordinates.

Use the explicit ordinary scalar-extension system and scalar/limit adjunction constructed for the sequence projection. Transport the system along the strict-system/sequence-site equivalence. The vertical unit comparison identifies its evaluation with the normalized scalar model. The scalar adjunction units give the ordinary unit equation, and the existing transition-on-pure-tensors equation gives the displayed coefficient transition. Identity and composition are already laws of the one strict system.

Take the resolving class of flat-term K-flat complexes over the cone ring. The K-flat resolution theorem gives a quasi-isomorphism from this class to every complex. Scalar extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes at every level, so the entire strict extension preserves them; the exact sequence-site equivalence preserves them as well. Apply the resolving-class left-derived construction on the homotopy category. Transfer its universal counit to complexes through the full object-surjective homotopy quotient. This gives one triangulated derived functor and one counit simultaneously before evaluation.

Map the ordinary evaluation isomorphism to cochain complexes, degreewise. After exact evaluation, compose the simultaneous counit with the exact-functor localization comparison and this cochain isomorphism. This counit and the level scalar-model counit are invertible on the same resolving class. The comparison-from-resolutions argument extends their quotient uniquely to a natural isomorphism of derived functors; its defining equation is exactly the representative square. Hence the comparison is natural on all localized morphisms, not only on chosen objects.
